Subject: Reserve options: minimum allocation ladder & activation sprint — NovumHealth

Elena / James —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As promised, attaching a concise set of dedicated reservation options that align with the usage profile you shared (peak inference during weekdays, heavy nightly batch embedding runs). The attached PDF (NovumHealth_Dedicated_Options_v3.pdf) shows three starter lanes plus two optional burst tiers. High-level summary below so the team can react quickly:

Option A — Conservative starter
- Baseline cluster: 24 GPUs (single-region us-west)
- Min-alloc guarantee: 8 GPUs (warm pool, reserved)
- Ramp: 24 -> 48 on month 3 if 60% utilization threshold reached
- Activation sprint: 14–30 day warm-up window

Option B — Balanced ramp (recommended)
- Baseline cluster: 48 GPUs
- Min-alloc guarantee: 16 GPUs
- Ramp: 48 -> 96 across a 60-day staged activation (30 days + evaluation + 30 days)
- Includes 10% warm capacity for burstable workloads

Option C — Growth-first
- Baseline cluster: 96 GPUs
- Min-alloc guarantee: 32 GPUs
- Ramp: immediate activation with phased traffic cutover and canary lanes

Key operational notes:
- Warm pool (min-alloc) keeps latency stable for cold-start sensitive workloads and reduces p99 spikes.
- We can pre-seed a small KV cache snapshot for your largest prompt sets during the sprint to reduce early token cost.
- Fallback policy: auto-route 10% of traffic to a quantized variant during capacity pressure; we can opt out if you prefer strict model parity.

Next steps I recommend: pick A/B/C (you can pick B with a smaller initial baseline if you want to stretch cash), confirm target go-live window (we proposed May 15 as a soft target in the doc), and we’ll lock SOW and Docusign link.

Attached: NovumHealth_Dedicated_Options_v3.pdf (proposal pages + concise activation checklist)

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30m call if you want to walk the numbers.

—Diego

Diego —

Thanks for the clear summary and the PDF. A couple of clarifying questions from our side before we loop in legal/procurement formally: 

1) During month 1 (initial sprint) what is the absolute minimum GPU footprint we would be charged for if utilization is low? Example: if we start Option B but average utilization is 10% month 1, how does the min-alloc guarantee apply to billing?
2) Can you confirm the time-to-scale SLA for the staged activation (if we trigger earlier than the 30/60 day plan)?
3) Are there credits for missed activation milestones (we have internal launch date constraints)?

James, copying procurement because they’ll want to drive contract terms and PO timing. Procurement, any scheduling constraints on your side?

Elena

Elena — quick answers inline and a proposal for a billing guardrail.

On 4/12/27 11:03 AM Elena Soto wrote:
> 1) During month 1 ... absolute minimum GPU footprint we would be charged for if utilization is low?

Short answer: you pay at least the min-alloc guarantee (16 GPUs for Option B) for the billing period. Practical note: we offer a one-time 30% ramp credit applied to the first 30 days of committed spend for new Dedicated customers to reduce burn during onboarding (we’ve applied this in previous deals). If you start with Option B and utilization is 10% we’d still charge for min-alloc but the ramp credit would offset O(30%) of that first month charge.

> 2) Can you confirm time-to-scale SLA if we trigger earlier?

We guarantee capacity to the baseline within 48 hours of a formal ramp trigger (subject to scheduled maintenance). For mid-ramp (e.g., 48 -> 96), we plan a staged 30/30-day window by default; if you need a compressed window we can provision accelerated activation with a one-time accelerant fee and a short-term burst reservation.

> 3) Are there credits for missed activation milestones?

Yes — we include service credits tied to onboarding SLAs for the activation sprint. The proposal doc’s Appendix B enumerates the credit schedule (we can highlight this page for procurement).

Operational suggestion: pick Option B but sign to a 48-GPU baseline with a 60-day optional activation to 96. We’ll include the 30% onboarding credit and a 14-day prewarm plan where our SREs seed the KV cache and create canaries. I’m attaching a short timeline spreadsheet that maps dates to milestones.

Attachment: activation_timeline.xlsx

Kimberly Park

Kimberly / Diego —

Procurement here. Thank you for the materials — two items we need prior to routing for signature: 

1) SOC 2 / security attestation and data handling appendix. Please include evidence or a pathway for on-prem KMS integration (we require customer-managed keys for PHI processing).
2) Our preferred procurement flow uses DocuSign and purchase order (PO). Please confirm if Redwood accepts PO + standard Master Services Agreement redlines (we have 3 small redlines on liability caps and data residency we’ll include).

Also, are there recommended milestones for invoicing vs. technical milestones (we prefer invoicing to align with go-live + acceptance sign-off).

Procurement team will be available for a 15m sync Fri 16th if helpful.

Thanks all — quick alignment from our side to unblock procurement: 

- Security: we will attach SOC 2 Type II summary and KMS integration notes in the contract appendix. We support customer-managed keys in our Private deployment and can document the network/VPC steps for a hybrid setup.
- Contract flow: we accept PO + DocuSign. We can accommodate the three redlines you mentioned; Diego/Kim will coordinate the specific language.
- Invoicing: Redwood recommends 30% upfront on signed commitment, 40% on baseline activation completion (baseline cluster live + acceptance run), and 30% on full ramp completion — but we are flexible to align with NovumHealth’s acceptance definitions.

If Novum can confirm Option B with a 48 -> 96 staged activation and agree to the 30% onboarding credit, I’ll ask legal to push a clean MSSA + SOW and send the DocuSign envelope (deal id RDW-2024-0492).

Karthik Iyer
